fact: PATNUC's account says a workshop of the project's stakeholders in Yaounde on 3 July 2025 discussed the diagnostic for updating the Plan Cameroun Numerique 2020, and that the next step could come after government approval; no updated plan is stated as adopted.

The ITU repository lists Digital Cameroon 2020 / National Digital Transformation Strategy as the country's strategy and says the countries it lists have adopted one; no adopting act is named, so this is dated by the repository's 2025 publication year.
The repository gives the time frame of Digital Cameroon 2020 / National Digital Transformation Strategy as 2016 - 2025.
The repository names MINPOSTEL as lead/owner of Digital Cameroon 2020 / National Digital Transformation Strategy.

The plan, dated May 2016 and prefaced by Prime Minister Philemon Yang as head of government, is called the adopted strategic plan in its monitoring section, with no adopting act named; it covers the digital economy, public administration and enterprises across all ministries.
The plan states its implementation is scheduled over five years, 2016-2020, with targets set for 2020.
The document is the plan's own full text, 72 pages, published on the MINPOSTEL site and a Cameroonian PDF copy.

The priority action plan lists projects per axis with baseline and 2020 target values, indicators, responsible bodies, priority and an amount in FCFA per project, for example 125,000,000,000 for a broadband backbone extension and 4,610,693,008 for a subscriber identification platform.

The plan assigns delivery to MINPOSTEL with the other ministries, ANTIC, ART and CAMTEL, and assigns monitoring and evaluation to the PPBS committees of each administration and their monitoring-evaluation cells.

The plan's financing column ties projects to domestic lines (BIP, the public investment budget, FST, the telecommunications special fund, and Budget de l'Etat) alongside FINEX external financing and some projects marked as funding sought.
Cameroon's PATNUC project unit at MINPOSTEL invited four shortlisted firms on 29 February 2024 to bid, by 2 April 2024, to update the 'plan numerique 2020'.

The minister said the draft national strategy for developing Cameroon's digital economy, built on the AI consultations, is being finalised, with pillars of infrastructure, data governance, skills, research and responsible AI.
